scope: Independent ISR/ABI source review plus linked CPU checks; not approval of newly authored public-fixture code
reviewed_contracts: Three enabled application IRQ sources: Timer0, USB, LED; callbacks use ordinary RET and immutable OEM wrappers provide the sole RETI.

Fixed priority within an active chain plus MCS51 in-service semantics limits nesting to distinct sources; summing all three callback/wrapper bounds does not assume a particular number of VS11 priority levels.
OEM wrappers preserve ACC, B, DPL, DPH, PSW and bank0 R0..R7. Bank0 is the compiler ABI; alternate banks may contain ordinary compiler data.
Timer/USB callback storage is nonoverlaid; shared foreground helper calls are confined to masked initialization.
Timer32 foreground access uses critical sections. Matrix snapshots mask LED IRQ and restore its prior enable. USB state transitions/publication use EA-preserving critical sections.
Flash IAP and loader-marker erase disable EA; failure paths restore saved IE, successful loader transition resets without re-enabling IRQs.
No new silicon-specific IRQ priority evidence was found; the existing explicit MCS51 architectural premise remains a premise, not a physical measurement.

primary_references.description: Original Intel MCS51 manual retained by existing architecture contract, printed pages 3-24, 3-25 and 2-65. Browser extraction unavailable due to 15 MB document size; existing report and source were reviewed.

SDCC compiler manual, sections3.7,3.8.1.1-4,3.8.2,3.9.1: nonoverlay, volatile/atomic shared state, stack/ABI and critical sections. Current manual is4.6.4; exact linked checks use project4.6.0 toolchain.

open_boundaries: Root must close foreground/startup proof and sum it with these61 bytes on each final image.
Physical peripheral timing/routing and VS11 silicon assumptions remain outside offline proof.
New fixture implementation needs independent review before commit.
